findings.artifact: documentary_hebrew p19; expanded p3, p18; documentary_parallel p33; expanded p11; night_expanded p5; documentary_hebrew p9
findings.detail: Some arrows repeat the same scan leaf: n42 twice on documentary_hebrew p19 and expanded p18, n33/n34 three times on documentary_parallel p33, n5 twice on the night pages. In every case I checked, the repeated arrow comes right after a conditional block (the Shabbat insertion, or the men's/women's benediction alternatives) with its label and rule. The scan guide says hidden conditional content must not suppress the next visible link, so the repeat is required. In the resolved profiles the repeat disappears: expanded_weekday p16 has a single n42 arrow where the Shabbat block is excluded. Expanded p3 also re-emits n24 where the text moves from the full-width Hebrew-only paragraph into the Hebrew column of the facing pair. This is consistent with tracking each column separately and is harmless. No arrow overlaps or is clipped. On night_expanded p18 the closest pair of arrows has a gap of about 9pt.

findings.artifact: documentary_parallel p32 (printed 24), expanded p9 and p15 (printed 7 and 13)
findings.detail: The English reads 'Torah to His people Israel .' with a space before the period. It appears the same way in documentary and expanded output, so it comes from the approved source text, not from rendering. I am not reopening the source here; I am only noting it.

The documentary parallel prints the identical English rubric in both columns ('In place of the preceding benediction women say:', 'In most communities of the German rite … (page 23) …'). This follows the two source pages and is consistent with the documentary design. The expanded profile shows it only once per language (expanded p11 has the Hebrew label in the Hebrew column and the English label in the English column), as the guide requires. Inside the Hebrew column the English rubric is right-aligned; it is readable, in correct LTR word order, and not clipped.
